assumptions: A variant is accepted only when every covering read agrees.
limits: Reads that do not align are reported, not forced; indels in low-quality ends are trimmed by the filter given.
bio.jane/contract.question: Where do this set of reads, aligned in one frame, differ from the reference, and what does each change do to the protein?

description: Compare a SET of sequencing reads against one reference in ONE shared frame: align every read to the reference, vote a consensus column by column, and report the positions where the reads differ from it, each with the change it makes to the protein. This is the whole-plate answer that grading reads one at a time cannot give — a variant is accepted only when every covering read agrees, so a single bad call does not become a mutation. Reads arrive as records or bases; the reference is the record this step runs on.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

end_phred.description: end trimming: the read becomes readable where three consecutive bases reach this score, and everything outside is masked. A Sanger read is unreliable at both ends by construction, which is why the ends are trimmed by RUN rather than per base. Only applies when quality_filter is true.

genetic_code.description: NCBI genetic-code table id, used to say what a variant does to the protein of a CDS on the reference. Advanced.

min_phred.description: mask any single base below this phred score. Only applies when quality_filter is true.

quality_filter.description: mask low-quality bases before the vote. Off by default, deliberately: a comparison shows what the FILES say before it shows what a filter says.

reads.description: the reads to compare — wire a batch of trace RECORDS in (their names come with them, and the per-read table is keyed by name), wire plain sequences, or name project documents.

name: compare_reads_to_reference

accepted.description: how many of those the vote accepted — every covering read agreed

alignmentFigure.description: the reference and every read in the shared frame, 80 columns around the first ACCEPTED change (else the first difference, else the start), shaded by column identity; draw_alignment draws any other window of `alignedReads`

cautions.description: every caution this comparison raises, each naming its own subject: uncovered stretches, reads that reach across only part of the frame, reads that dissent from the accepted consensus, insertions the reads could not resolve, mixed peaks

conclusion.description: the run's headline in one sentence, generated from THIS result and identical to the words the panel shows

consensus.description: the voted consensus as a sequence, gaps and unresolved insertions removed — the sequence to hand on

coveragePct.description: how much of the reference any read covers at all

derivation.description: the chain behind the numbers: what identity was measured over (and that an indel does not lower it), the unanimity rule, how one frame came out of N pairwise alignments, the quality gate, the genetic code and the inputs

gaps.description: stretches of the reference no read covers, as 1-based inclusive runs. A clean comparison over 60% of a construct is not a verified construct, and this is the half that says so

identityPct.description: of the covered columns, how many match the reference

perRead.description: each read's own coverage, identity and substitution / deletion / insertion counts, plus how often it disagrees with the accepted consensus — the row that says WHICH read is the problem

record.description: the consensus as a linear record, ready for any downstream step

variants.description: one row per column where a read differs from the reference: its position, the reference base, the voted base, whether the vote ACCEPTED it, the coverage behind it and the consequence for the protein
